chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a group of travelers on a road who were ambushed; they captured the bandits, and some of the travelers testified for others. He said: 'Their testimony is not accepted unless there is a confession from the bandits or testimony from others against them.'

31 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), 'Is the testimony of the executor (al-wasi) for the deceased accepted regarding a debt he has against a man, along with another just witness?' He replied (with his signature): 'If another just witness testifies with him, then the claimant must take an oath.'

And I wrote, 'Is it permissible for the executor to testify for the heir of the deceased, whether young or adult, regarding a right the heir has against the deceased or against others, while he is the one holding the property for the young heir but not for the adult?' He replied: 'Yes, it is appropriate for the executor to testify to the truth and not withhold the testimony.'
And I wrote, 'Is the testimony of the executor accepted against the deceased, along with another just witness?' He replied: 'Yes, after an oath.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting the testimony of an executor (wasi) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the evidentiary standards for testimony, specifically addressing the validity of witnesses among travelers who apprehended bandits, which requires either the bandits' confession or independent corroboration. It further details the legal capacity of the deceased's executor (*al-wasi*) to testify for heirs or against the deceased, emphasizing that his testimony is accepted alongside another just witness, subject to the claimant's oath. These rulings highlight the Shia juristic emphasis on procedural fairness and the specific role of the executor in preserving the rights of minors and adults alike.
